Definition: from G4012 and G2224; to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively):--gird (about, self).
BiblicalUsage: Perizonnymi means to gird all around, to fasten a belt or girdle. Jesus tells His disciples to have their loins girded about and their lights burning, Paul tells believers to stand with their loins girt about with truth, and John sees the risen Christ girt about the breast with a golden girdle.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that being girded is being ready: truth fastened around me like a belt, so I can stand and work and watch for the Lord's coming.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
